floater.title: Welcome to Stellarys Viewer
floater.text: Please read the project information and privacy policy below. Continue opens the sign-in screen. This is separate from Second Life's Terms of Service.
floater.text_editor:
Before installing Stellarys Viewer
This software is not provided or supported by Linden Lab, the makers of Second Life.
Stellarys Viewer is an independent, non-commercial hobby project based on Firestorm 7.2.4.80712. It is also not provided or supported by the Firestorm team.
- Support: use GitHub Issues: https://github.com/NekoMisa/stellarys-viewer/issues. The maintainer helps as time permits; there is no guaranteed response time. Do not include credentials, private chat or unredacted logs in public issues. - Privacy: read the Stellarys privacy policy: PRIVACY.md before installing. The policy covers local files, Second Life statistics, inherited network services, GitHub update requests and voluntary support submissions. - Extra features: the AMD fix changes rendering on affected meshes. Posing other avatars requires explicit permission and a compatible viewer (Stellarys or Black Dragon). Resulting poses are local, not synchronised. Shot presets restore camera/lens/blur, local lighting and snapshot dimensions in the original region; they do not restore poses or save/upload a photo. - Limitations: this is a hobby viewer with an older Firestorm base, not guaranteed to have the fixes/features of the latest official viewers. Linux builds are experimental. Windows is x64 with AVX2; Linux is native x86_64. Builds are unsigned. SHA-256 verifies integrity, not publisher identity. - Content and controls: the viewer can access user-created Second Life content, including Moderate/Adult content where your account is permitted. Inherited optional RLVa features let compatible scripted content restrict controls and may be used with adult content. Follow Second Life's maturity, permissions and conduct rules; the viewer does not grant extra access rights. - Installation and updates: installation is user-directed. Update downloads and installation require approval. Link registration is optional. Separate settings/cache are preserved on updates and by default on uninstall; see the platform guide for removal choices. Other viewers' profiles are not removed.
Read and comply with the Third-Party Viewer Policy: https://secondlife.com/corporate/third-party-viewers, Linden Lab Terms of Service: https://lindenlab.com/tos and Second Life Terms and Conditions: https://lindenlab.com/legal/second-life-terms-and-conditions. The viewer retains the server-directed Terms-of-Service acceptance flow. Directory listing and Linden Lab approval are not claimed.
Stellarys Viewer privacy policy
Effective date: 10 October 2026. Maintainer: NekoMisa.
Stellarys Viewer is an independent hobby project based on Firestorm. This software is not provided or supported by Linden Lab, the makers of Second Life. This policy describes the Stellarys Windows and Linux builds; services reached through the viewer have their own privacy policies.
Information on your computer
The viewer stores preferences, account identifiers and optional saved sign-in information, chat/diagnostic logs, cached world content, browser data, poses and shot presets on your computer. Saved sign-ins are optional. Chat logging and other privacy options are available in Preferences. These files may contain avatar names, conversations, locations and technical information. Protect your Windows/Linux account and review files before sharing them.
Windows normally uses %APPDATA%\Stellarys_x64 and %LOCALAPPDATA%\Stellarys_x64. Linux normally uses ~/.stellarys_x64. Cache, chat logs and snapshots can use locations you select instead. Updates preserve this data. Windows uninstall preserves it by default and offers explicit removal options. Linux package removal/purge preserves home-directory data; remove your Stellarys profile and any custom data locations yourself if wanted. Neither installer requires a Second Life account or password.
Second Life and network services
Connecting sends authentication information to Linden Lab's login service and exchanges account, avatar, location, inventory, chat and world data with Second Life as needed to operate the viewer. The inherited viewer statistics packet sends session/performance information, viewer version, operating system, CPU, GPU, memory, network and device identifiers to Linden Lab. This is separate from any analytics operated by the Stellarys maintainer.
The inherited Firestorm functionality can request configuration, compatibility and support data from Firestorm/Phoenix services, including at startup. Recipients can see your IP address, request headers and viewer/browser identification. Some inherited endpoints use HTTP rather than HTTPS. These services are operated by their respective providers, not by Stellarys.
Optional voice, parcel media, web pages, search, translation and external links contact the selected providers. They can receive your IP address and information needed for the feature, such as requested URLs, voice traffic or text submitted for translation. Embedded web content can store cookies/browser data locally. Use Preferences to control media, voice and related privacy choices. A manually selected alternative grid receives the information required to log into that grid; do not reuse your Second Life password on an untrusted grid.
See Linden Lab's privacy policy: https://lindenlab.com/privacy and the policies of the services you choose to use.
Update checks and downloads
The bundled updater requests release information and approved downloads from GitHub over HTTPS. GitHub and its download infrastructure receive normal network information, including your IP address and updater user agent. The updater does not send your Second Life credentials, chat logs, settings or cache. Startup checks can be disabled; manual checks remain available. Downloading and installing an update require your approval. Downloads and updater preferences are stored locally. See GitHub's privacy statement: https://docs.github.com/en/site-policy/privacy-policies/github-general-privacy-statement.
Posing, photographs and support
Posing another avatar uses explicit permission requests and acceptance/revocation messages through Second Life IMs. Consent state is kept in memory for the current session/region. Pose changes are local to the viewer applying them; they are not broadcast as animations or synchronised with other viewers. Poses and shot presets can be saved locally. A snapshot is uploaded or shared only when you choose a viewer action that does so.
The Stellarys additions do not operate a separate maintainer analytics or automatic crash-upload service. Diagnostic files can still be created locally. Support requests are voluntary. GitHub Issues, comments and attachments are public; do not post passwords, saved sign-in files, private conversations or unredacted logs. Technical information sent to another resident through the inherited support feature requires your approval.
The maintainer can read and use information you deliberately submit to the project to investigate issues and discuss development. Public submissions may remain in GitHub history and copies held by others. Do not assume that deleting a comment removes every copy. GitHub handles its own account and hosting data.
Contact and changes
For privacy questions, contact the maintainer through Stellarys GitHub Issues: https://github.com/NekoMisa/stellarys-viewer/issues without including sensitive information. Ask for a private contact method before sharing any private details. Support is provided as time permits, without a guaranteed response time. Changes to these practices will be documented in this policy and relevant release notes. This policy does not claim Linden Lab approval or replace the policies of external services.
